exposure: preferred language (American Sign Language, English, or bilingual)
age of onset of hearing loss
self-reported quality of perinatal care communication
cohort: Deaf and hard-of-hearing (DHH) individuals in the U.S. who gave birth within the past 10 years; sample predominantly white, college educated, and married.
finding: The study found no evidence supporting differences in obstetric outcomes among DHH birthing people across medical factors related to deafness, except for poorer perinatal care communication quality being associated with higher prevalence of preterm birth and NICU admission.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth was reported by 31% of the sample, but no significant differences were found across outcome variables with respect to mode of delivery.
gest_age: Preterm birth was assessed as an outcome
birth_weight: Low birth weight was assessed as an outcome
